subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Hayes <stephanie.hayes@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking & next steps

Hi Stephanie — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

TL;DR
- Baseline forecast: ~200M tokens/month with seasonal peaks up to ~1B tokens/month.
- Target unit economics: Acme indicated a goal of $100–$150 per 1M tokens (target $/1M) as acceptable for long-term pricing.
- Redwood preliminary benchmark: effective delivered price (post-caching & batching) "target" of $125 per 1M tokens for generation-heavy workloads; raw list comparators below.

Key points from our discovery:
- Workload mix: ~70% generation (chat/completion), ~20% embeddings, ~10% reranking/other.
- Average request length: 1.5k tokens, with many repeated prefixes (good candidate for prefix/KV caching).
- Regulatory: data residency required in us-east-1 and SOC2 evidence requested.

Preliminary benchmarking ($ per 1M tokens) — ballpark for comparison purposes only:
- OpenAI (hosted, generation) : ~$220 / 1M tokens
- Anthropic (hosted) : ~$210 / 1M tokens
- Self-hosted on third-party hosts (with aggressive quantization + managed infra): ~$90–$140 / 1M tokens (infrastructure + ops overhead varies widely)
- Redwood (delivered target with batching/caching/quantization applied): $125 / 1M tokens (provisional; depends on committed volume and prefix-hit rate)

Important notes on the numbers:
- The "effective" $/1M depends a lot on cache hit rates and batching windows. For Acme's workload, we expect prefix caching to reduce generation token counts by ~30–45% on common flows — that lowers the effective unit cost materially compared to raw per-token list prices.
- Dedicated reservations and a 12–24 month committed volume contract would meaningfully reduce list price (we can show tiered pricing in the attached sheet).

Next steps I propose:
1) I attached a brief pricing spreadsheet (redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx) with tiered examples for 200M / 500M / 1B monthly committed volumes and an effective-price worksheet that models cache hits.
2) Attached benchmark deck (benchmark_vs_openai_anthropic.pdf) with methodology and test harness notes.
3) If helpful, Aditya can run a quick PoC on a subset of traffic to validate effective token counts and latency impact (should take 2–3 weeks).
4) Can we schedule a pricing review with your finance/procurement folks next week? I can bring Marissa (pricing) and Aditya (SE).

Open items for your team to confirm:
- Are the volumes above (200M baseline / 1B peak) reasonable?
- Any must-have security controls beyond SOC2 + US residency?
- Procurement timeline & PO process (required to shape discounts).

Thanks — I'll follow up with the attachments and a calendar invite once I hear your preferred slots.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-08-15T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens benchmarking & next steps

Thanks Vanessa — helpful summary and appreciated the quick turnaround. A few clarifying notes: 

- Volumes: 200M baseline sounds right; we'll need to confirm peak cadence but 1B during launches is realistic.
- Target price: finance will want a firm quote that shows committed-tier pricing and examples of how prefix caching impacts the effective $/1M. Please include the assumptions / cache-hit model in the workbook.
- Security/regulatory: SOC2 is required; we also need confirmation that data can be restricted to our VPC in us-east-1 for the Private option (if we go that route).
- Procurement: timeline is 6–8 weeks for initial contract review (legal + security). We need an SOW and a standard contract redline to start.

Can you provide a formal quote (PDF) and an editable SOW we can share with procurement? Also include any options for dedicated capacity vs hosted (and the delta in $/1M).

If you can get those docs over tomorrow, I'll route to procurement and schedule an internal sync.

Thanks — Stephanie
Director of Product, Acme Robotics
stephanie.hayes@acmerobotics.com | (617) 555-0199
